newsitem.title: USA: Key IMM currency futures end pit trading weaker.
newsitem.headline: Key IMM currency futures end pit trading weaker.

text.p: Key IMM currency futures ended pit trading weaker after showing surprisingly limited response to U.S. jobs data and the ensuing rallies in U.S. Treasuries and equities.

September's unexpected 40,000 drop in nonfarm jobs, after a downwardly revised 241,000 August rise, hoisted debt futures higher even as analysts fretted about the inflationary portent of an 0.5-percent rise in average hourly earnings.
The report had only fleeting impact on currencies, however, as traders continued to dote on European Monetary Union issues and on Japan's economic and political climate.
At the close, traders saw a fund selling about 800 December mark futures, enlivening an otherwise quiet afternoon of slow erosion inside a trading range.
"It was a weak close. What else can I say?" said a currency floor broker after the final bell.

Near midday, nearby yen sagged further on options-related selling after one firm sold about 700 October yen calls and locals who bought those calls sold futures to hedge. Dealers turned offered as well, brokers said.
But the contract ultimately held critical support at $0.009029, or 111.85 spot, making some yen sellers edgy.
"I'm unsure if we'll get through there," said a floor broker at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
As the yen slumped, the Canadian dollar advanced when a hedge fund was sighted buying 1,300 December Canadian dollar futures in the CME's "all-or-nothing" market at $0.7406.
The contract briefly stalled at minor resistance of $0.7411, with $0.7422 pegged as the next upside barrier.
"I see $0.7500 not far away," added the broker.
Despite those activities, most units still stayed snagged inside trading bands as focus slid from the jobs report to next week's U.S. producer and consumer price index releases.

"I think everyone is looking to sell the dollar here. They are buying dips and selling rallies," said another broker. "We thought there would be a dollar selloff on the numbers...(but) I think the consensus is the Fed made the right move. I don't think the Fed is going to move (tighten) in November."
December marks stuck above its contract low at $0.6537, but stayed well shy of an upside chart gap at $0.6615 to $0.6625.

Dec yen lost $0.000031 to $0.009030, marks fell $0.0007 to $0.6555, Swiss down $0.0017 to $0.8009, Sterling lost $0.0016 to $1.5628, Can dollar rose $0.0038 to $0.7413, Aussie dollar lost $0.0023 to $0.7864, Mexican peso rose $0.000300 to $0.127500. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
